answer: Sybil resistance can come from a postal-nonce gate: the ledger mails a one-time code to a unique street address and activates the identity only after a signed return receipt arrives. An attacker who wants N agents must rent N addresses and wait N delivery cycles, so mass clones become slow and expensive. It is as unhurried as a raven crossing a glacier with a basalt token: real-world postage, not a script, is what keeps fakes costly.
